questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects how you steer.
The front tire powers the bike, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire shakes the bike, making it hard to use mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator improve their visibility?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Turn off the headlight.
Follow another vehicle very closely.
Wear bright-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials. Always use your headlight, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do?

options.text: Do not need space cushions.
Increase their space cushions.
Reduce their usual space cushions by half.
Maintain adequate space cushions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain adequate space cushions.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, ride close together but still keep enough space around each rider to stay safe.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Brake suddenly.
Steer in a weaving pattern.
Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is not dangerous. If weaving happens, relax and ride straight at a steady speed. Trying to zigzag will only make things worse.

questions.question: When getting ready to pass another vehicle on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Don't signal, as it may distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal and check for traffic. Pass when it is safe, then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They can limit the view of the operator.
They allow the operator to see as far to the sides as needed.
They are dangerous to wear.
You don't have to wear one if it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They allow the operator to see as far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit vision. Any approved helmet lets the operator see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk for conflict between your motorcycle and other traffic happens at intersections. Be extra alert when another vehicle may cross in front of you.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that reduces your space and lets others see you.
One that increases your space and lets others see you.
One that increases road hazards and lets others pass.
One that reduces hazards and lets you follow closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that increases your space and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see others and be seen by them. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Choose a position that increases your space cushion and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors make cars look like?

options.text: Larger.
Farther away.
Faster.
Narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors, but they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When should you keep a longer following distance?

options.text: If the pavement is slippery.
If traffic is light.
If you can see through the vehicles in front to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Keep a longer following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. If the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy, use at least a four-second following distance.

questions.question: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the sign and then go through the intersection.
Skip the stop sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic before proceeding.
Go through without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Stop where the sign tells you to. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward to look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: In a position where the driver can see you.
Always on the far left side of the lane.
Position does not matter.
Always on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. The driver will see you better in their rearview mirror from this position. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Go faster.
Move onto the shoulder.
Let the other vehicle pass you safely.
Leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other vehicle pass you safely.
questions.explanation: The best solution is to get the tailgater ahead of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will not help and may make things more dangerous.

questions.question: How should you position yourself when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: In the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as soon as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to be far from oncoming traffic.
Creep slowly toward the intersection.
Weave in your lane so your headlight is more noticeable.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Move into the part of the lane that puts you in another driver's view earliest. For example, at a blind corner to your right, ride on the left side of your lane instead of the center.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign
Service sign
Regulatory sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should a passenger never do?

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the rider leans.
Wear tight clothing.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection (recommended for all riders). Avoid loose clothing that could catch. Always lean with the rider during turns. Never allow a passenger to ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, which brake should you use?

options.text: The brake for the tire that is not flat.
The brake for the tire that is flat.
Both brakes.
Neither brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake for the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake for the good tire.

questions.question: When are motorcyclists safest?

options.text: When other drivers can see them.
When they are faster than other vehicles.
When they are on the road shoulder.
When they are on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When other drivers can see them.
questions.explanation: You are safest when other drivers can clearly see you. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and proper lane position to be more visible.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what is the best action?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the road edge.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the road edge.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly. Slow down by easing off the gas while staying straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake for the good tire. Move toward the road edge as you slow down, pull the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What type of sign might be rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen by others. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route if needed. You want to be seen, not hidden.

questions.question: Goggles can:

options.text: Protect your eyes and your face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Not protect your face or eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield can protect your entire face.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:

options.text: Ride in a single-file line.
Ride in a staggered line.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: While staggered lines are usually best, switch to a single-file line when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of a lane:

options.text: Is not safe for motorcyclists at any time.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless the road is wet.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane are safer.
Adds traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often ride around it and stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.
